`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Taint and typestate both run the policy's preparation (selector compile, binding) before any unit's read capture opens. Taint makes up for this by replaying the saved compile reads into each unit through the `replay_preparation_reads` hook. Typestate keeps the no-op default, so its ROOT ledger only shows what the solve itself read.
- That is why the coordinator said "a current object hash alone is not enough". The policy hash covers the protocol text, but not what the selector chose over the current workspace. Only a replayed read of the selection makes a later change to it invalidate the ROOT product.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

#9017 is confirmed by reading the code. The saved whole-evaluation key never includes the semantic lowering identity. Before choosing a fix, I'll look at where the key's epoch is computed and where the adapter versions live.

#9017 is confirmed by reading the code on master. Saved policy unit keys and whole-evaluation keys never include the semantic lowering identity. So after a change that bumps only an adapter version, with no policy epoch token, the saved whole-evaluation result can be replayed stale. No test has shown this at runtime yet.

My fix decision: fold each language's active adapter version, plus the IR version, into the one epoch that both kinds of key use. Every lowering change already has to bump its adapter version for semantic artifacts, so policy answers will then be invalidated without anyone remembering a policy token. I rejected the other option, storing read receipts on evaluation rows: it needs a schema change and adds no safety, because lowering changes only arrive with a new binary.

Child `378913fe` is implementing it in its own worktree. Its brief includes a regression test, the update to `cache-identity-levers.md`, and the policy-integration suite. I sent the design to 5992a for review.
